title: Resource Ribbon & Burst Scenario Canvas for Dedicated Capacity
creator: Asha Kapoor
description: Design a compact, horizontally-scrolling 'Resource Ribbon' for the Dedicated capacity view that surfaces pool health, cost signal, and fast actions (autoscale tweaks, burst scenarios, failover) while keeping the main dashboard uncluttered. Add a connected 'Burst Scenario Canvas' modal that lets operators compose, preview cost/latency impact, and schedule bursts or canary rollouts. Work focuses on hi-fi prototypes, accessibility, and clear handoff tokens for engineering. The ribbon must support: 1) quick single-click actions with confirm flows, 2) lightweight health miniatures (sparkline + KPIs), 3) on-hover detail card with recent incidents and suggested remediations, and 4) cost impact previews before committing burst/autoscale changes.
acceptance_criteria: Ribbon renders correctly at 3 breakpoints (desktop, tablet, narrow desktop) and is horizontally scrollable when pools overflow
Each pool card shows name, short health sparkline, current GPUs in use, requested autoscale state, and estimated cost delta for next 1h
Burst Scenario Canvas supports creating, saving, and previewing a scenario with duration, target throughput, and cost estimate
Quick actions initiate an audited request (with confirmation) and emit the expected SDK event (documented action payload) for backend wiring
Design tokens and accessibility contrast meet AA for all primary states and keyboard-only navigation is supported
decisions: Persist ribbon order by 'last-updated' with manual pinning option to keep operator-chosen pools visible
Use a two-tier visual density: condensed pool chip for list view and expanded card for focused view to reduce cognitive load
Expose cost delta in-line using a tiny currency chip, and provide an explainable tooltip linking to the cost model doc
Leverage existing console color tokens; introduce one new 'burst intent' accent token for temporary state
tradeoffs: Inline cost estimates are approximate and may diverge from billing; chosen in favor of faster operator feedback versus absolute accuracy
Keeping the ribbon compact reduces immediate incident context compared to a full panel; mitigated by on-hover detail cards and a linked full 'Pool Details' page
Single-click quick actions increase risk of accidental changes; mitigated via short confirmation modal and an undo window
